name: energy_pairs_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: India's energy sector has a natural upstream-downstream split: upstream producers (ONGC, Oil India) benefit from high oil prices, while downstream refiner-marketers (IOC, BPCL, HPCL — the 'OMCs') are hurt by high crude because their retail margins get squeezed (government-regulated fuel prices lag crude movements). This creates a NEGATIVE correlation between upstream and downstream on days with significant crude price movements. The pairs trade: when Brent crude moves sharply intraday, go long upstream + short downstream (if crude rises) or vice versa. The inefficiency exists because: (1) retail traders trade all 'oil' stocks the same way, not distinguishing upstream from downstream, (2) the negative correlation only manifests with a 10-20 minute lag as the market processes the crude-margin implication, (3) on non-oil-move days, the stocks are positively correlated (sector sentiment), making the signal regime-dependent.
universe: ONGC, Oil India (upstream), IOC, BPCL, HPCL (downstream OMCs), Reliance (refiner but not OMC)
stock_filter: ONGC: ADV > ₹100 crore. IOC/BPCL/HPCL: ADV > ₹50 crore each

other: Brent crude futures 1-min data (MCX or ICE)

conditions: brent_change_bps > 50 (crude rising — bullish upstream, bearish downstream)
up_down_spread < 10 bps (spread hasn't widened yet — upstream hasn't outperformed)
long.confirmation: up_down_spread starts widening (crosses above 5 bps from below)

conditions: brent_change_bps < -50 (crude falling — bearish upstream, bullish downstream)

entry.entry_price: market order both legs: long upstream + short downstream (crude up) or vice versa

exit.target: up_down_spread reaches ±25 bps (full crude impact priced in)
exit.stop_loss: up_down_spread moves 15 bps against position (wrong direction on crude impact)
exit.trailing_stop: 8 bps trailing after 15 bps spread movement achieved
exit.signal_exit: crude_regime changes to 'non_oil' (crude move reverses, thesis invalidated)

filters.time_filter: no trades first 15 min or last 15 min
filters.trend_filter: trade direction must align with crude price direction
filters.event_filter: skip on OPEC meeting day, Indian fuel price revision day (OMC margins directly affected)
other_filters: skip if crude_regime is 'non_oil' (no crude catalyst, upstream-downstream correlation is positive, not negative)
skip if government announces fuel price change today (OMC margins directly reset)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — the upstream-downstream margin dynamic is structural. Until Indian fuel pricing is fully deregulated (unlikely politically), OMC margin squeeze during crude spikes will persist.

weaknesses: The crude_regime threshold (50 bps = 0.5% intraday crude move) may not be reached on most days. The strategy fires only on significant crude move days (~30% of trading days).
Government fuel price interventions (price cuts before elections, subsidy changes) can flip the upstream-downstream dynamic unexpectedly.
ONGC's gas business and Oil India's exploration portfolio mean they're not pure crude oil plays. The upstream-downstream model is an approximation.
prior_art: Energy sector pairs trading is well-established in US markets (XOP vs XLE). Driesprong, Jacobsen & Maat (2008) 'Striking Oil: Another Puzzle?'. In India, PPAC (Petroleum Planning & Analysis Cell) data on OMC under-recoveries provides the empirical basis for crude-margin inverse relationship.
notes: Reliance Industries should NOT be included in the downstream group because its refining margins are market-linked (GRM = gross refining margin, not regulated). RIL is a refiner, not a marketer, and its margin dynamics differ from OMCs. Brent crude data on MCX (CRUDEOIL contract) is available via Kite API for commodities.
